Twenty-eight comments

This was composed by Tommy Peoples.

↳ Posted by SPeak on October 12th, 2002.

What key do folks play this in?

I really like this tune, but there’s no way I could play it in F up to speed on my keyless flute… does anyone play it in G in sessions?

↳ Posted by Q on November 22nd, 2005.

In G

Yep, I play this one in G in the sessions. pretty much as lunasa play it. It wouldn’t be too friendly on my pipes otherwise.

↳ Posted by Amckay on October 4th, 2006.

G?

Yeah, G is more common. Though I always relish a chance to play it if F if there are no flutes or pipes around. It really is loads better in F on the fiddle. Partly because you can roll the high third (A, when in F) on the fiddle. Pipes and flutes obviously have no problem rolling their top B

COMMENT:

Peoples Tune

This comes off of a CD that Brad Hurley sent me containing a famous session tape from Gort in 1991. Brad added some tracks at the end that feature Kevin Crawford conducting a workshop that usually involves sitting and listening in amazement as he plays. Someone had the good sense to switch a tape recorder on and capture this tune that I’ve never heard anywhere else. If someone has a name other than what Kevin referred to it as, please elucidate.

Here’s a link to an mp3 I made of the tune:
http://www.tipsyhouse.com/Peoplestune.mp3

This tune submission is in response to this discussion:
https://thesession.org/discussions/18336
